description.p: Shotpad takes a screenshot and gives you everything you need to make it presentable: padding, gradient or image backgrounds, rounded corners, drop shadows, a subtle tilt, and a full set of annotation tools.

ul.li: Text labels with an outline or a background plate
Auto-incrementing numbered badges for step-by-step guides
Blur, pixelate or block out anything private

Grab text: drag a box over any writing in the picture and it is copied to the clipboard, in English, Turkish, Azerbaijani or Russian. Text you have redacted stays hidden. Nothing is sent anywhere - the recogniser runs on your machine and needs no network.

description.p: Capture works the same on GNOME, KDE Plasma, XFCE and MATE, on both X11 and Wayland. Shotpad talks to the XDG desktop portal where that is the only option, and falls back through grim, the desktop's own screenshot tool, maim, scrot and ImageMagick as needed. Area selection always uses Shotpad's own overlay, so the experience does not change when you change desktops.
New Grab text tool: drag a box over any text in a screenshot and it is copied to the clipboard. English, Turkish, Azerbaijani and Russian are included, and text you have redacted stays hidden.

Screenshots can now wear an outer border: a mat between the picture and the background, in frosted glass, white, smoke or black. The glass preset fades across the diagonal so it catches the light rather than sitting as a flat wash.
Fixed the sidebar scroll bar being unusable in a small window, where the window's own resize edge took the pointer instead.
The tool rail now names every tool beside its icon. The button at the top of the rail collapses it back to icons only, and the choice is remembered.
The eraser can now clear an area: drag a box over several marks to remove them all at once. Clicking a single mark still works as before.
Blur, pixelate and block-out now show the effect live while you drag the region out, instead of only once you release the button.
The Copy and Save buttons now confirm what they did: the button turns green and reads Copied or Saved for a moment, instead of leaving you to guess whether the click registered.
Fixes screen capture on X11 when the desktop font size has been raised: the screenshot was painted shrunk into a corner, and window highlights were offset and too large.
